name: curve bends one CC through a table of points
about: curve on CC 74 maps its value through four points by straight lines between them, ties away from zero, and holds the end values outside the first and last point.
notes: points (16,4) (32,9) (96,120) (112,127), cc 74 (4A). For x between two points (x0,y0) and (x1,y1): y0 + round((x - x0) * (y1 - y0) / (x1 - x0)), round to nearest with ties AWAY FROM ZERO, in integers, as `scale` does it.

Below the first point the value is the first point's out, above the last it is the last point's out. x is found in the first segment whose right end is at or above it, so a value ON a point gives that point's out from either side.

t 0: x 8 (08) is below 16, CLAMPS to the first out 4 = 04. THE FIRST OUT WAS 0 UNTIL THE SABOTAGE RUN OF 2026-10-04, and then a core that extrapolated below the first point (4 - 8 * 5 / 16 = 1.5 here) floored at 0 and read the same as the clamp, so the clamp was not graded.
t 1: x 16 (10) is the first point: 4 = 04.
t 2: x 24 (18), segment 16..32: 4 + 8 * 5 / 16 = 4 + 2.5, a TIE, away from zero 4 + 3 = 7 = 07. Truncating gives 6, ties to even gives 6.
t 6: x 120 (78) is above 112, CLAMPS to the last out 127 = 7F. An extrapolating core floors this at 127 too, so this step does not grade the top clamp. Vector 25 does, where the last out is 120.
NEGATIVE CONTROL t 7: CC 7 is not CC 74 and passes unchanged, B0 07 18. Curved it would read B0 07 07.
NEGATIVE CONTROL t 8: a note is not a value, 90 3C 18 passes unchanged.
NEGATIVE CONTROL t 9: a bend passes unchanged because the op names a CC, E0 00 18.
NEGATIVE CONTROL: l2 lists its points with the inputs going DOWN (64 then 32) and is refused bad-args. Inputs must rise strictly.
NEGATIVE CONTROL: l3 has 17 points, inputs 0, 7, 14 up to 112, each one valid, and is refused bad-args, since a table holds at most 16.
NEGATIVE CONTROL: l4 has one point and is refused bad-args. A curve needs two.

NEGATIVE CONTROL: l6 has an out of 128 and is refused bad-args. Every in and out is 0..127.
